column2: “Something's wrong. {n2},
you look ill.”
I said firmly.
“Really, it's nothing.”
“But…”
“I overdid it skiing.{r}{p}I'm just a little tired.”
She tried to force a smile.
Maybe I shouldn't press any further.
Maybe the word 'kamaitachi' brings back some bad memory for her.
Everybody has one or two memories like that.
The truly considerate thing would be not to ask.
But I'm a little curious.
What could {n2}'s bad memory of 'kamaitachi' be?
Wait a second.
What was a kamaitachi, anyway?
I tilted my head.
Right, now I remember.
I think we ate it in school lunch in elementary school.
So {n2} couldn't eat her 'kamaitachi' and got scolded by the teacher.
And now that memory is coming back to her…
“Being picky about food isn't good.”
I scolded {n2} gently.
But {n2} had a look on her face like, what is he suddenly talking about?
Oops.
Maybe it wasn't something you eat.
Right.
This time I really remembered.
I think it was a phenomenon where a whirlwind or something makes a vacuum and causes cuts.
People in the old days blamed it on a weasel-like animal with a sickle, which is how it got that name, right?
But what kind of bad memory could she have of that?
Maybe she got cut somewhere?
“Poor thing…{r}{p}Did it hurt?”
{n2} was still tilting her head.
Wrong again?
What on earth is it?
I don't know.
It bugs me like crazy and I still don't know.
Forget it.
Thinking is getting to be a hassle.
I'll just ask {n2}.
“What's your bad memory of kamaitachi, {n2}?”
“My bad memory of kamaitachi?{r}{p}
What are you talking about? I don't have one.{r}{p}You've been saying nonsense for a while now…”
Huh…?
I decided to ask Keiko.
“Hey,
do you know who's staying near your room?”
I thought I'd spoken to her normally, but she lowered her head and didn't answer.
Is she terribly shy?
I had no choice but to repeat the same question to Aki.
Oh well, I gave up.
There's still tomorrow.
With that thought, I took a quick shower, turned off the light, and climbed into bed.
“Hehe.
Of course.”
She giggled, and for some reason poured the wine in her hand into her cleavage.
“Oh no,
I spilled it.”
Spilled it?
It looked to me like she'd poured it on purpose…
“That feels awful.{r}{p}Could you undo the zipper in the back?”
She stood up and turned her back to me.
I pulled the zipper down as she asked.
When she slipped her arms out, the dress dropped to the floor.
Now she was in only knee-high stockings, a garter belt, and panties.
Wine ran from her chest down her belly and thighs, leaving red stains on her white underwear.
“I'm all wet and it feels awful.{r}{p}Could you lick it clean for me?”
My head felt paralyzed.
I leaned in as she asked and ran my tongue over her skin.
From her diaphragm to her navel, and then her thighs…
As I lapped up the wine like that, my consciousness began to blur
and I collapsed onto the bed.
“No,
I don't care about her.{r}{p}You're much nicer.”
They were words I didn't mean, but saying them, I started to really believe it.
“Really?{r}{p}
I'm happy even if it's flattery.{r}{p}…Hey,
let's have fun together tonight.{r}{p}Okay?”
“Have fun…”
“Oh, stop playing dumb.{r}{p}You know what I mean.”
She jabbed me in the ribs with her elbow.
“Find a new employer?”
“Yes!{r}{p}
Having worked for the Eastern bloc for so long,

'Kamaitachi' must still hold a lot of important information, even now that US-Soviet tension has eased.{r}{p}It must include key secrets about the Self-Defense Forces and US forces in Japan.{r}{p}To get that kind of information
, plenty of countries would pay any amount.”
I took out the paperback I'd brought to read if I had spare time.
I had stuffed it in with my pile of unread books in a hurry, so I checked the title first.
It was Stephen King's 'The Shining.'
I'd thought it would be perfect to read in the snowy mountains.
…I decided not to read the paperback.
There was a magazine in the room, so I decided to read it from cover to cover.
I couldn't stop thinking about the body, and nothing sank in.
But as I struggled like that, morning slowly drew closer.
Just before six, I couldn't stand it any longer and decided to go downstairs.
“I'm just a student.
I'm not a spy or anything.”
“Oh, really.
Not a spy.{r}{p}Then it's none of your business.”
“Right.
It's none of my business.”
“…Like I'd believe that!{r}{p}Who'd go out of their way to say they're not a spy?!”
My face was ground harder into the floor.
“It's true!{r}{p}
I'm really not a spy!{r}{p}They just mistook me for one!”
“Mistook you?
Who mistook you for what?”
The question flew at me sharply.
“A woman from French intelligence seems to have thought I was 'Kamaitachi'…”
In my terror, I blurted everything out.
“And?”
“She used seduction to make me drink a truth serum, but when I came to she had her throat cut and was dead, and Mr. Kobayashi and the others said not to call the police…”
Mikimoto's body on top of me grew heavier and pressed down on me.
“It-
it hurts…
I'm telling the truth, so please get off…”
A voice that wasn't Mr. Mikimoto's reached me.
“Men who talk too much are unpopular.”
Twisting my neck, I saw {n2} standing there.
I kicked at the ice pick.
A powerful kick would send Aki Kawamura's ice pick flying…
or so I'd thought.
In reality, my kick cut through thin air, the slipper slid off and hit the ceiling directly above, then flew back over my head.
“Ugh!”
I heard a strange groan behind me and turned to see Keiko Kitano standing frozen, covering her eyes.
In her gloved hand she held something like piano wire.
She had been about to attack me from behind when the slipper hit her directly, and she seemed to have flinched.
A blessing in disguise, as they say.
I grabbed her arm and tried to twist it up.
The next moment, the room spun around, my back slammed to the floor, and I couldn't breathe.
I had no idea what had happened.
It felt like I'd been thrown with an aikido move.
She looped the piano wire around my neck from behind as I lay there, and began to tighten it.
I jammed my fingers between the wire and my neck, but the skin seemed to split at the slightest touch.
It was like a blade!
“I'm coming too.”
I didn't want to be left behind in a place like this.
I figured it was safer to stay with {n2}.
“Okay…
then…”
{n2} whispered something to Midori.
“Come on,
let's go.”
She said that and tugged at my arm.
“W-what about Midori?”
“…I'm having her look after those people.”
She glanced toward the bathroom and whispered in my ear.
“Look after…”
“We lock them in there and put them to sleep with knockout gas.{r}{p}Now,
let's go find Uncle.”
We went down to the first floor and decided to check the basement.
The door leading underground wasn't locked.
{n2} went down the stairs cautiously.
“Is h-he down here?”
“…I don't know.{r}{p}But I can't think of anywhere else.{r}{p}…Uncle?{r}{p}
Are you there?”
There was no answer to {n2}'s call.
Just then, I felt something hard pressed against my back.
“Keep going down, nice and easy.”
I heard a lazy voice with a Kansai accent {C3}(the Osaka area){C0}.
We understood the situation and raised our hands.
“You two, go down quietly.{r}{p}Try anything funny and the kid's heart gets two holes.{r}{p}One where the bullet goes in, and one where it comes out.”
{n2} walked slowly down the stairs without taking her eyes off me.
I looked around the basement, but there was no sign of anyone, not Mr. Kobayashi or anybody.
With my hands still raised, I turned slowly: Mr. Kayama was sitting on the stairs, pointing the gun at us.
“Now, which one of you is 'Kamaitachi'?”
“'Kamaitachi'?{r}{p}
What are you talking about?”
{n2} played dumb.
“…No, you two aren't 'Kamaitachi.'{r}{p}…Are you working for the government?”
Seeing {n2} fall silent, Kayama grinned.
“Guess I hit the mark.{r}{p}I see, so that's it…
Then 'Kamaitachi' is probably…”
That was when it happened.
From somewhere in the inn came a pop like a firecracker.
For a moment Kayama took his eyes off us and looked up at the ceiling.
Then {n2} threw a bottle from the wine rack at Kayama's face.
“Whoa!”
The heavy bottle hit Kayama's elbow, fell, and shattered, splashing wine everywhere.
By the time he aimed the muzzle at us again, {n2} had already circled behind him and chopped the back of his neck.
Kayama slowly crumpled into a sea of wine.
As I stared blankly, {n2} called to me irritably.
“Hurry!{r}{p}
We have to get 'Kamaitachi'!”
what about him?”
“He won't wake up for a while.{r}{p}Now,
hurry!”
I went around Kayama and chased after {n2}.
“Get 'Kamaitachi,' you say…{p}who is it, anyway?”
“Not the Kayamas, not the office ladies, not Mikimoto…{p}that leaves only one person, doesn't it?”
“So it is Tanaka…?”
{n2} nodded.
Upstairs, {n2} went straight to Mr. Tanaka's door without hesitation and knocked.
It's now or never, I thought, and lunged for the gun.
I felt as if a red-hot skewer had been run through me, and slowly sank to the floor.
Huh…?
Something hot gushed out over the hand pressed to my chest.
My…
blood?
Listening to the sounds of the two of them struggling, I rolled onto my back on the floor.
An overwhelming drowsiness swept over me.
I heard {n2}'s voice calling out.
“Why…
why did you do something so reckless?”
was crying?
She had only brought me along as camouflage.
Hadn't she thought it didn't matter who died as long as the mission was done?
…Was she crying for me, {n2}?
I moved my mouth, but no voice came out.
Just before I closed my eyes and surrendered to sleep, I felt something dripping onto my cheek.
It was warm, like spring rain…
“Come with me.”
I played tough.
I seized the arm of Mr. Tanaka, who was peeking out from behind the bed.
“Ow, ow, ow,
don't pull so hard…”
Ignoring his words, I walked past Midori and led him out into the hallway.
Wasn't his outfit strange?
He was dressed too lightly to go out into this blizzard.
“{n2}, this is weird.”
I whispered in her ear and quickly told her my doubt.
{n2}'s expression changed in an instant.
Toshio was just opening the back door, about to push Mr. Tanaka out into the blizzard.
“Stop right there.”
{n2} had somehow drawn a gun and had it aimed precisely at Toshio's back.
I ran over to Toshio.
“No!”
By the time {n2}'s voice reached me, it was already too late.
The moment I stepped out the door, it felt like countless punches were coming at me
Stabbing punches and heavy body blows gouged my flesh and destroyed my organs…
It was as if bombs buried all over my body were bursting one after another.
A spray of blood filled the air with a red mist.
The smell of gunpowder stung deep in my nose.
As someone's anguished scream reached me, I slowly fell on top of Toshio.
Am I…
going to die?
In a place like this deep in the mountains, riddled with machine-gun fire, without my parents or friends ever knowing…
For a moment, a silence so deep it was maddening settled in.
Again that anguished cry, and then gunfire like a sewing machine.
Another shower of blood rained down.
Whose blood was this…?
The thud of someone falling.
Someone called me, barely breathing.
Is it {n2}?
Trying to save me…?
Someone was crawling across the floor, reaching a hand toward me.
A bloodied hand.
Summoning all my strength, I reached out and clasped that hand…
“…Sorry,
but I don't want to die yet.”
Avoiding {n2}'s eyes, I said it.
{n2} looked just a little sad, and smiled.
“…I see.
Of course.
Nobody wants to be shot like a dog in a place like this without knowing why.{r}{p}…All right.
{n1}, stay in some room and keep still.{r}{p}Block the door with a bed or something so it can never be opened.{r}{p}I'll definitely come back, so wait until then.{r}{p}Okay?”
let's escape together!”
“I have a duty.
Don't worry.{r}{p}Trust a professional.”
With one last smile, she stood up.
At my call she didn't even turn around, but dashed out the back door and vanished into the blizzard.
I felt as if I'd done something irreversible.
But what could I, an untrained, carefree student, have done?
I'm not wrong,
I'm not wrong, I told myself as I went upstairs.
Mikimoto might still be in my room, so I decided to shut myself in {n2}'s room.
I locked the door and moved the bed in front of it.
I closed the curtains and, without turning on a light, crawled into bed and kept waiting.
About five minutes later…
I thought I heard a gunshot in the wind.
And then a sound like a machine gun.
…Maybe it was my imagination.
An hour passed, then two.
{n2} would definitely come back.
I believed that and kept waiting.
I put my hands around her waist as if hugging her hips.
When I tried to hold on tight, my crotch inevitably pressed against {n2}'s rear.{g}
This is bad.
I slid my hands toward her belly and shifted position so our hips wouldn't touch.
“Impossible!{p}
There's no way I can do that!”
“Then do you have a better idea?”
“We have no choice!”
“…All right.”
I said reluctantly.
